messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: gdistsamp starting values
parts:
Dear Andy and all developers of unmarked,

thank you for this great package! I started to use gdistsamp() but I noticed there are
problems with convergence, and it is recommended to provide starting values
using the `starts` argument. Is there any documentation or description of
the format of the `starts` argument? I.e. which parameters in which order and
which format. It will probably depend on the mixture and keyfun settings and
number of covariates as well (I normally use "P" and "halfnorm", but general description
would be welcome).
I could try to hack the source code but I feel safer asking.

Thanks and best regards!

        Tomas

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] gdistsamp starting values
parts:
hi Tomas,
This never seems obvious to me so the few times I've been interested in this question for other functions in unmarked I always wind up having to double check by peeking at the code.... but it seems like the order is the same as the parameters of the print-out: abundance, availability, detection... I confirmed this by looking at the negative logliklihood function which is this: (notes off to the right)

nll <- function(pars) {
            lambda <- exp(Xlam %*% pars[1:nLP] + Xlam.offset)      # Here the first 1:nLP elements are extracted for 'lambda'
            if (identical(output, "density")) lambda <- lambda *
                A
            if (T == 1) phi <- matrix(1, M, T) else {
                phi <- plogis(Xphi %*% pars[(nLP + 1):(nLP +            # Here the next few elements of pars are extracted for phi
                  nPP)] + Xphi.offset)
                phi <- matrix(phi, M, T, byrow = TRUE)
            }
            rate <- exp(Xdet %*% pars[(nLP + nPP + 1):(nLP +       # Finally we get the last pile of estimates of "p"
                nPP + nDP)] + Xdet.offset)
            rate <- matrix(rate, M, T, byrow = TRUE)

regards
andy

Hi Andy,

thanks! I have few more questions:

1) are intercepts involved there as well? Are they situated before the
coefficients? I mean like:

starts = c(intercept for lambda, coefficients for lambda, intercept for availability,
coefficients for availability, intercept for detection, coefficients for
detection)

2) Are there no other parameters besides abundance, availability,
detection predictors? Like N[i] - latent abundance on site i, or some other
parameters (e.g. for negative binomial, overdispersion etc.)?

Thanks,

        Tomas

 there are no other parameters unless you fit a Negative binomial distribution in which case I believe the LAST value of the parameter vector is log(size)

andy
